originalSourceText:
Q.7   Consider the following interaction:
       User: “I enjoy playing the piano.”
      Robot: “Is the piano your favorite instrument?”
      Match the AIML tags in Column I with the corresponding example/function in
     Column II.

      Column I — AIML Tag  Column II — Example related to the interaction

        P. <category>              1. "Is the piano your favorite instrument?"

       Q. <pattern>                2. Hiddenly stores "your piano" as the conversational
                                  context

       R. <template>              3. Complete conversational rule containing the trigger
                              and response

        S. <set_it>                  4. "I ENJOY PLAYING *"

     Which of the following gives the correct matching?

      (A) P–3, Q–4, R–1, S–2

      (B) P–3, Q–1, R–4, S–2

      (C) P–2, Q–4, R–1, S–3

      (D) P–4, Q–3, R–1, S–2

       Explanation:
      <category> → complete conversational knowledge unit
       <pattern> → trigger/input pattern
      <template> → programmed response
       <set_it> → stores the processed value in conversational context
      The structure follows the AIML pattern-matching and context-memory example.
      Refer slide 14 of Lecture 49: Conversational AI & Human-Robot Interaction
